blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH, THEN OF ALL ISRAEL · UNITED KINGDOM
David. Seven years in Hebron, thirty-three in Jerusalem.
House of David 3rd of 4 in The united kingdom
✓ Did right “David did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded…”
THE UNITED KINGDOM: 4 RULERS SAUL → SOLOMON
Samuel anointed David, Jesse's youngest son, at Bethlehem “in the midst of his brethren”, while Saul still reigned. 1 Samuel 16:1–13
After Saul's death David asked the LORD where to go, went up to Hebron, and “the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah”. 2 Samuel 2:1–4
After Abner and Ish-bosheth were dead, the tribes came to Hebron; David “made a league with them”, and “they anointed David king over Israel”. 2 Samuel 5:1–3

Chronicles tells only this last anointing, “according to the word of the LORD by Samuel”, and lists the armed men of every tribe who came to Hebron “to make David king over all Israel”. 1 Chronicles 11:1–3 1 Chronicles 12:23 1 Chronicles 12:38
From the textSo 1–2 Samuel record three anointings: by Samuel at Bethlehem, by Judah at Hebron, and by Israel's elders at Hebron. 1 Samuel 16:13 2 Samuel 2:4 2 Samuel 5:3
ON THE WORLD STAGE: The Philistines · Aram (Zobah and Damascus) · Hamath · Ammon · Moab and Edom · Tyre · Geshur · Amalek
“David did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite”
Kings' verdict names its one exception: “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite”. 1 Kings 15:5
Nathan gave him the LORD's sentence for that act: “the sword shall never depart from thine house”. David answered, “I have sinned against the LORD”. 2 Samuel 12:9–13
After the census he said, “I have sinned greatly in that I have done”. 2 Samuel 24:10
Kings measures later kings by him: Solomon's heart “was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father”. 1 Kings 11:4 1 Kings 14:8
Chronicles gives the reason David might not build the temple: “Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars”. 1 Chronicles 22:8 1 Chronicles 28:3
In Acts, Paul quotes God's word about him: “I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart”. Acts 13:22 1 Samuel 13:14

Zadok and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were the priests. 2 Samuel 8:17

Chronicles describes the Levites' music before the ark and their courses, set up by David; a later king followed “the commandment of David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet”. 1 Chronicles 15:16 1 Chronicles 16:4–7 1 Chronicles 23:1–26:32 2 Chronicles 29:25

Thirty years old at accession; seven years and six months in Hebron; thirty-three years in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:4–5).
King of Judah at Hebron 1010 BC; of all Israel 1003 BC; died 970 BC (McFall). Young (2003) puts Solomon's first official year in 972 or 971 BC, overlapping David's last.

Albright dated the division of the kingdom to 922 BC. Scripture's forty years for Solomon then put David's death about 962 BC. Albright's own figure for David's accession was not checked for this page.
King in Hebron 1055 BC; over all Israel 1048 BC; Jerusalem taken 1047 BC; Solomon made king 1015 BC. Ussher has David live about six months more and die in 1014 BC.
Piscator, Clericus, Michaelis, Movers and Thenius, and Keil himself (tr. 1866)

The two verses differ by a few Hebrew letters. Keil held that 2 Samuel was miscopied from a text like Chronicles', so Elhanan killed Goliath's brother Lahmi; David killed Goliath. 2 Samuel 21:19 1 Chronicles 20:5 1 Samuel 17:49–51 [5]
Bertheau and Böttcher, as reported by Keil (1866)
They held that Chronicles altered a reading that said Elhanan killed a giant named Goliath, out of offence at the clash with 1 Samuel 17.[5]

Scripture does not name David's mother.
Scripture does not give his age at his first anointing or when he fought Goliath.
Apart from his first year in Hebron, his move to all Israel after seven and a half years, and his death in his fortieth year, Scripture does not say in which year of his reign most events happened.
Scripture does not say how long Absalom's revolt lasted.
No outside record from David's own lifetime names him.

From the textThe site's family data lists “Nahash” as one of David's parents. That is STEP Bible's reading of 2 Samuel 17:25, where Abigail, sister of Zeruiah, is called “the daughter of Nahash”; Chronicles calls Zeruiah and Abigail David's sisters. Scripture names Jesse as David's father and does not name his mother. This page does not rely on the Nahash link. Ruth 4:17 2 Samuel 17:25 1 Chronicles 2:13–16
